source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text:
Mature fruit should be harvested by cutting the stalk cleanly with a sharp knife or pruning tool and lowering it carefully by hand or into a catching net, never by letting it drop or fall to the ground, since impact damage from a fall bruises the flesh and can split the husk, both of which sharply reduce market value and shelf life -- allowing fruit to fall and be picked up off the ground is described as a practice to avoid in managed orchards, in contrast to how durian sometimes naturally sheds fruit in the wild.

After harvest, durian fruit is typically left to ripen off the tree at room temperature for a period of about several days (commonly cited in regional literature as roughly 4-8 days depending on variety and maturity at cutting) before the flesh reaches full eating ripeness, softness, and aroma; fruit cut too early (before reaching physical maturity) will not ripen properly off the tree and should be discarded rather than sold, since underripe durian does not develop good flavor or texture no matter how long it is stored.
